data: 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 上手[じょうず]に 話[はな]せる ようになるには、 丁寧[ていねい]な 話[はな]し方[かた]や くだけた 話[はな]し方[かた]、 敬語[けいご]と いった スピーチ レベルが 違[ちが]う 話[はな]し方[かた]の 練習[れんしゅう]も しなければならない。
In order to improve one's skill in speaking Japanese, it is necessary to practice speech styles in a variety of different registers, from polite speech to casual speech to honorific speech.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

Phr1(、Phr2,~)といった {N/NP} [in this structure, Phr could also be a sentence] "like; such as N" といった X is used to present examples of X. X is always a noun or noun phrase. といった may be preceded by nouns, noun phrases and sentences. * If preceded by nouns, 2+ nouns are presented ** If preceded by sentences or phrases, only one sentence or phrase is presented. などのN and のような N are similar in meaning, but they are usually not preceded by sentences.
大学[だいがく]で 一生[いっしょう] 懸命[けんめい] 勉強[べんきょう] するのは いい ことです。 しかしながら、 宿題[しゅくだい]や 研究[けんきゅう]ばかりで、 友達[ともだち]も できないのは よく ありません。
It's a good thing to study hard in college. It's not good, however, to spend all your time with homework and research and not make any friends.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1. しかしながら S2. "however, but" しかしながら is a disjunctive conjunction and appears only in sentence-initial position. It is a highly formal expression and is used typically in written language.
日本[にほん]の スポーツ クラブの 先輩[せんぱい]と 後輩[こうはい]の 関係[かんけい]って 面白[おもしろ]いね。 山田[やまだ]： うん、 ああ いう 関係[かんけい]って、 他[た]の 国[くに]では あまり 見[み]られないだろうね。
The senpai/kohai relationship in Japanese sports club is interesting, isn't it? Yamada: yeah, that sort of relationship is probably not something you really see in other countries.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) When そういう, こういう and ああいう refer to something/someone the speaker sees or perceives, they are used for something/someone close to the hearer, close to the speaker, and away from both the speaker and the hearer respectively. (2) These phrases are also used to refer to something/someone the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned. Specifically, そういう is used when the speaker has just mentioned something/someone. こういう is used when the speaker has just stated something factual about something/someone. And ああいう is used when the information the speaker or the hearer has just mentioned is known to both. --- 英訳 [English translation]: that/this kind of; such --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {そう/こう/ああ}いうN
初[はじ]めに 砕[くだ]けた 話[はな]し方[かた]で 日本[にほん]語[ご]を 覚[おぼ]えてしまった 人[ひと]は、 助詞[じょし]を よく 間違[まちが]える 傾向[けいこう]が ある。
People who first learned to speak Japanese through casual speech have a tendency to make frequent mistakes with particles.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain.nonpast (という)傾向がある。 Means: Have a tendency to; have an inclination to; There is a tendency to; tend to This construction is used when someone or something has a tendency to do something. It is commonly used in written language and formal speech. という is optional.
日本[にほん]の 代表[だいひょう]的[てき]な 伝統[でんとう]系[けい] 能[のう]に、 能[のう]と 狂言[きょうげん]が ある。 前者[ぜんしゃ]は 悲劇[ひげき]で 後者[こうしゃ]は 喜劇[きげき]だ。
Among the traditional performing arts of Japan are Noh and Kyougen. The former is a tragedy and the latter is a comedy.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
前者は（〜）{V-te/A-te/ANa で/N で/}、後者は〜 "The former ~, and the latter ~" This sentence structure is used to refer separately to the two things, people, etc. mentioned in the previous sentence.
留学[りゅうがく]中[ちゅう]、 沖縄[おきなわ]を 除[のぞ]く 日本[にほん] 全国[ぜんこく] 各地[かくち]を 友達[ともだち]と 一緒[いっしょ]に 旅行[りょこう] した。
WhileI was studying in Japan, I travelled everywhere but Okinawa.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 を除く N2 "except (for); with the exception of ~; but ~" 除く means "to remove; get rid of." を除いて is used as a compound particle meaning "except."
手塚[てづか] 治虫[おさむ]が 描[えが]いた 漫画[まんが]では 「ジャングル 大帝[たいてい]」や 「ブラックジャック」が 人気[にんき]が ある。 前者[ぜんしゃ]は 白[しろ]い ライオンの 話[はなし]で、 後者[こうしゃ]は どんな 病気[びょうき]でも 直[なお]す ことが できる 医者[いしゃ]の 話[はなし]だ。
Among the manga Tezuka Osamu wrote, Kimba the White Lion and Black Jack are popular. The former is the story of a white lion and the latter is the story of a doctor who can cure any disease.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
前者は（〜）{V-te/A-te/ANa で/N で/}、後者は〜 "The former ~, and the latter ~" This sentence structure is used to refer separately to the two things, people, etc. mentioned in the previous sentence.
今[いま]、 見[み]た ビデオから、 文楽[ぶんらく]や 歌舞伎[かぶき]は 江戸[えど] 時代[じだい]に 一般[いっぱん]の 人々[ひとびと]にも 広[ひろ]がったと いう ことが 分[わ]かります。 さて、 次[つぎ]に 紹介[しょうかい] するのは、 これも 江戸[えど] 時代[じだい]に 一般[いっぱん]の 人[ひと]にも 楽[たの]しまれる ようになった 茶道[さどう]です。

We understand from the video we've just watched that bunraku and kabuki became popular among the common people, too, during the Edo Period. Now, the next thing I'm going to introduce is the tea ceremony, which also became popular among commoners during the Edo Period.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

(S1.) さて、S2. "well; now; well now" さて always occurs at the beginning of a sentence and signals that (a) the speaker/writer is beginning a new topic (the new topic and the previous topic may be part of the same discourse) (b) the speaker/writer is going to ask a question about the information just provided, AS SEEN HERE or (c) the speaker is leaving. さてis not used in casual situations.
宮崎[みやざき]駿[しゅん]の アニメって、 いいよね。
As for Hayao, Miyazaki's anime, they're good aren't they?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is a colloquial topic marker. It often appears in questions. In written language, は can be used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Speaking of ~, As for ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N って
綺麗[きれい]な 目[め]を した 人[ひと]。
The person with pretty eyes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This pattern is used to describe a feature of someone or something, focusing on a certain part or attribute of the person or thing. -- When the phrase modifies a noun, した is commonly used instead of している. Synonyous with N1はN2がAdj. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 は Adj+N2 をしている b. Adj+N2 をした N1
嬉[うれ]しい ことに、 奨学[しょうがく]金[きん]が もらえる ことに なった。
Happily, I ended up being able to get a scholarship.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

A.plain.non-past ことに “It is~ that~; I am/We are ~ that ~; To my ~" ことに is used to express the speaker's feeling or subjective judgment about what is said in the main clause. ことに can only be used with a limited set of words.
この 建物[たてもの]は できたばかりだから、 新[あたら]しくて、 とても 綺麗[きれい]だ。
This building has just been built, so everything (inside) is new and clean.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.past ばかり indicates that someone has just done something or something has just happened. The noun modification form is ばかりの. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have just V-ed --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.past ばかりだ V-plain.past ばかりの N
Ａ: 明日[あした]から 春休[はるやす]みなんです。 Ｂ: ああ、 それで、 みんな 嬉[うれ]し そうにしているんですね。
A: Spring break starts tomorrow. B: Oh, so that's why everyone looks so cheerful.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: It is a sentence-initial conjunction. It precedes a fact, conclusion, decision, etc. S1 is the cause/reason for the information stated in S2. それで cannot be used when S2 is the speaker's judgement, request or command. In this situation, だから should be used. Note that だから can be used in situations where それで is used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: because of that; so; that's why; for that reason --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ S１。それで、S２。
来年[らいねん]、 日本[にほん]に 行[い]ける ことに なってので、 嬉[うれ]しくて しょうが ない。
I can't even tell you how happy I am because I can go to Japan next year.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-te しょうがない "cannot help V-ing; cannot stop feeling ~; so ~; unbearably ~" てしかたない、てしようがない,etc. literally mean that a situation is such or is occurring and there is no way to escape it. The phrases are used to indicate that the speaker is unable to control his psychological/physiological reactions or bear a sensation or an external situation. しょうがない i s the colloquial version. This use is different from the following example, where the しかたがない means "it cannot be helped; there's nothing one can do." お金がないのだから、留学できないのはしかたがない。
この オペラ 歌手[かしゅ]は、 本当[ほんとう]に 綺麗[きれい]な 声[こえ]を していますね。
This opera singer has a really pretty voice, don't you think?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This pattern is used to describe a feature of someone or something, focusing on a certain part or attribute of the person or thing. -- When the phrase modifies a noun, した is commonly used instead of している. Synonyous with N1はN2がAdj. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 は Adj+N2 をしている b. Adj+N2 をした N1
アニメが 好[す]きな 若者[わかもの]で、 宮崎[みやざき]駿[しゅん]の アニメを 見[み]た ことが ない 人[ひと]は いない。
There's no young person who likes aime who hasn't seen Hayao Miyazaki's films.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V−nai ない N は{ない／いない} Means: There is no N which/who does not V This construction is used to create sentences containing double negatives. VないNは(い)ない is equivalent to "All Ns V."
「隣[となり]の トトロ」でも、 「風[かぜ]の 谷[たに]の ナウシカ」でも、 宮崎[みやざき]駿[しゅん]の アニメは みんな 素晴[すば]らしい。
From "My Neighbor Totoro" to "Nausica and the Valley of the Wind", (no matter the choice) all of Hayao Miyazaki's anime are superb.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 でも N2 でも "including X and Y; whether (it is) X or Y" This is used to provide examples for the statement in the sentence. This structure implies that there are also things other than the examples which make the statement true. Note that XもYも (both X and Y) does not carry such an implication..
京都[きょうと]は 古[ふる]い お寺[てら]が 有[あ]るだけでなく、 綺麗[きれい]な 景色[けしき]でも 有名[ゆうめい]です。
Kyoto is famous not just for its old temples, but also for its beautiful scenery.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The sentence structures ~だけでなく、~も, etc. expresses the idea "not only X, but also Y." Particles に, へ, で, と or から may appear before も. --- 英訳 [English translation]: not only ~, but also ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Noun だけでなく、Noun(Particle) も b. Subject だけでなく、Noun(Particle) も: Type 2c
4[よん]年間[ねんかん] 頑張[がんば]って 勉強[べんきょう] して、 ついに 卒業[そつぎょう]に 日[ひ]が 来[き]た。 嬉[うれ]しいけれど、 ちょっと 寂[さび]しい。
I spent four years studying hard, and now graduation day has finally come. I'm happy, but it's kind of a sweet yet sad feeling.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The adverb ついに indicates that something happens or something expected doesn't happen, after waiting for it, longing for it, expecting it to happen, making an effort to make it happen, or after struggling/suffering in a hard situation for a long time. --- 英訳 [English translation]: at last; finally; in the end; after all --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ついに
大阪[おおさか]、 京都[きょうと]、 それに 奈良[なら]にも 行[おこな]った。
I went to Osaka, Kyoto, in addition to Nara.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: それに is used to add an item or make an addition statement. --- 英訳 [English translation]: in addition; moreover; furthermore; what's more; on top of that; and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. N1 {、/と / に} N2, それに N3 b. S1。それに、S2。 c. S1 し、それに、S2。
東京[とうきょう]、 大阪[おおさか] ともに 外国[がいこく]人[じん]が 多[おお]い 町[まち]だ。
There are a lot of foreigners in both Tokyo and Osaka.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1,N2 共（に） "Both N1 and N2" The colloquial form is N1もN2も.
大阪[おおさか]まで 新[しん]幹線[かんせん]で 行[い]きたいんですが、 いくらでしょうか。
I would like to go as far as Osaka by bullet train, but how much does it cost?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: S んだけど／ですが is used as a preliminary remark by the speaker to inform the hearer of the speaker's desire, the current situation, etc. before (a) asking a question related to that desire, (b) asking for an opinion on the matter, or (c) making a request. This phrase can also be used to extend an invitation or an offer. When making a request, the request is often unstated, as shown below. んだけど is more casual than んですが. --- 英訳 [English translation]: but (in english, null in most situations) --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 〜ん{だけど/ですが}
シート ベルトの おかげで、 大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]でした。
Thanks to the seatbelt, I was ok.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N {の/じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} おかげ "because; due to" Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result. Both おかげ and せい are dependent nouns indicating cause. The former is used when the cause brings about a desirable result, and the latter when the cause brings about an unwanted result.
誰[だれ]かが ドアを ノック した ような 気[き]が するから、 ちょっと 見[み]てくれない？
I think someone may have just knocked on the door, so could you go and check?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

~(ような）気がする Meaning; I feel that~: I have a feeling that ~; have the impression that ~; it seems to me that~ It indicates that the speaker is not certain about something, but has the feeling that it's true. ような can be dropped without changing the meaning.
せっかく ケーキを 焼[や]いたのに、 誰[だれ]も 食[た]べてくれなかったから、 がっかり した。
I went to all the trouble to bake a cake but no one would eat it - it was so disappointing.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

せっかく V {のだから/のに} "with effort; at great pain; take the trouble to do ~; ~, which is a rare occasion/event/etc." せっかく is used in 2 situations: (1) when the speaker/writer does something with a lot of effort or at great pain ad therefore he/she wants to make use of it; or, in spite of the effort or pain, he/she cannot make use of it. (this is the case here)
鍋[なべ]に、 だいたい 3[さん]分[ぶん]の 2[に]ぐらいまで、 水[みず]を 入[い]れてください。
Please fill the pot about two/third full with water.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
だいたい number/amount "approximately number/amount" だいたい means "most;almost; nearly(all); approximate." The meaning changes depending on what だいたい modifies.
明日[あした]なら 大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]です。
If it's tomorrow, I can make it (it's alright).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: なら is used when the speaker supposes that something is the case or is true and makes a statement, suggestion, etc. based on that supposition. の occurs before なら when the supposition is based on what the speaker has heard from someone or learned from the situation. Nなら means "if it is N; N would/could ~." In "S1 なら S2", the action/event in S1 does not have to take place before that in S2. --- 英訳 [English translation]: Nなら = would; could~ S(の)なら = if (it's the case that) ~; if (it's true that) ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~(の)なら
寿司[すし]が 好[す]きな 人[ひと]も いるし、 嫌[きら]いな 人[ひと]も いる。
There are people who like sushi and there are people who don't like sushi.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1も V-plainし N2もV Means: some do ~ and others do ~; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; do ~ and ~ among other things, and more (pg 142 in とびら）
寿司[すし] 好[す]きな 人[ひと]も いれば、 嫌[きら]いな 人[ひと]も います。
There are people who like sushi and there are people who don't like sushi.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1も V-conditional, N2 も V。 Means: some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well. This sentence structure is used to present some members in a group, things in a category, actions someone takes, characteristics of something/someone, etc. among others. Although the form of the verb here is conditional, the meaning is NOT conditional in its usage.
もし、 タイムマーシンが あると したら、 どの 時代[じだい]に 行[い]って、 誰[だれ]に 会[あ]ってみたいですか。
If you had a time machine, what era would you go to and who would you want to meet?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

（もし）S としたら Sとしたら literally means "If I/we/you suppose that S." This construction is usually used to present a hypothetical situation, but can be used for an actual situation as well in which the speaker is presenting the situation as if it were hypothetical in order to indicate something indirectly. もし here is optional. It emphasizes that the speaker is presenting the situation as a hypothetical one.
この 子[こ]は 赤[あか]ちゃんの 頃[ころ]は よく 泣[な]いていたが、 4[よん]歳[さい]に なって、 あまり 泣[な]かない ようになった。
When he was a baby he used to cry a lot, but since he turned four he doesn't cry so much any more.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ようになる indicates a gradual change over a certain period of time; it means that someone (or something) comes to the point where he/she does (or can do) something or does not (or cannot) do something. V-なくなる is synonymous with V-ないようになる. The difference is that the latter implies a more gradual change. --- 英訳 [English translation]: come to (be able to) V; not V now; not V any more. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.non-pastようになる (V is often the potential form)
あなたに とって、 一番[いちばん] 大切[たいせつ]な 人[ひと]は 誰[だれ]ですか。
Who is the person that's most important to you?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Xにとって means "to X; for X" in a context where something (or someone) is important to X, or is necessary, useful, good, difficult, etc. for X. X is often a person, a geographic unit or an organization. --- 英訳 [English translation]: for, to, from the standpoint of, as far as ... is concerned --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nに取って
子供[こども]の 頃[ころ]は、 兄弟[きょうだい]と よく 遊[あそ]びも すれば、 けんかも した ものだ。
When we were children, I used to play with my siblings a lot, and I used to fight with them, too, sometimes.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

V1-masu もすれば、V2-masu もする "some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well" This structure is used to present actions or states (usually 2) as examples of possible or past actions/states. In many cases the actions/states are contrastive ones.
この カメラでなら、 誰[だれ]でも、 一応[いちおう] きれいな 写真[しゃしん]が 撮[と]れる はずです。
With this camera, anyone should be able to take a decent picture.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

一応 "for the time being; for now; tentatively; although not perfectly; sort of; just in case" In this sentence the use means "tentatively" 一応 is used when an action/state is tentative or not quite complete, perfect or satisfactory. It is also used when an action is taken as a precaution.
こんな まずい 料理[りょうり]を 美味[おい]しいなどと 言[い]ったのは 誰[だれ]だ？ (=～などと いう ことを)
Who was it that said unappetizing food like this was delicious?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) Sentence など(は) is an abbreviated form of S などということは, which means "things like S." (2) Noun など(は) is a shortened form of Noun などという{もの/人/etc.}は, which means "things/people/etc. like N." なんで is a colloquial version of など(は). (3) When S is a quotation, Sなどと is an abbreviated form of S などということを. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/people/etc. like ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N{など(は)/なんて}: 子供{など(は)/なんて}
あの 車[くるま]は、 3[さん]， 4[よん]日[か] ずっと 家[いえ]の 前[まえ]に 止[と]まっている。 いったい 誰[だれ]の 車[くるま]なんだろうか。
That car's been parked in front of my house for three or four whole days. Who on earth does it belong to?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
Number1, Number2 + Counter "(2 or 3) days/times/etc.; (3,4) hours/cars/etc." Two successive numbers are used to indicate an approximate number or amount
A: 今[いま]、 誰[だれ]か ここに 来[き]ませんでしたか。 B: ええ、 ちょっと 前[まえ]に サラリーマン風[ふう]の 人[ひと]が 来[き]ました。
A: Was there someone here just now? B: Yes, a little while ago someone who looked like an office worker came by.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 風の N2 "~style; ~type; look like" 風 is a suffix and is added to nouns to make no-adjectives. X風 means "X style/type" or "looks like X"
私[わたし]は ウニ 以外[いがい]の 寿司[すし]は、 何[なん]でも 食[た]べられる。
I can eat any sushi except sea urchin.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{N1/DemP} 以外の N2 "but; except; other than; besides" X以外のY means "Y, excluding X." のY is often omitted.
次[つぎ]に 発表[はっぴょう] する 人[ひと]は、 誰[だれ]かと いうと、 田中[たなか]さんです。
The next presenter is… um… it's Ms. Tanaka.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{いつ／だれ／どのぐらい} かというと "to tell you when/who/etc.~ (it is ~)." Question word + かというと literally means "if I were to tell you who/what/when/etc." In general this phrase is used to emphasize the information which follows or to delay providing the information in order to keep the hearer in suspense or to stall while recalling it.
この ゲームは 子供[こども]から 大人[おとな]に 至[いた]るまで、 誰[だれ]でも 楽[たの]しめます。
Anyone can enjoy this game, from children (all the way) to adults.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 から N2 に至まで "from N1 all the way through N2; from N1 to even N2." This construction indicates a span of time or space and emphasizes the size of that span at the same time. It can also be used for other than spatial or temporal spans, as seen here. Primarily used in written language.
この 頃[ころ] 前[まえ]より 日本[にほん]語[ご]が 話[はな]せる ようになってきた ような 気[き]が します。
Recently, I've felt like I can speak Japanese better than I could before.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

~(ような）気がする Meaning; I feel that~: I have a feeling that ~; have the impression that ~; it seems to me that~ It indicates that the speaker is not certain about something, but has the feeling that it's true. ような can be dropped without changing the meaning.
日本[にほん]に 来[き]たばかりの 頃[ころ]は、 日本[にほん]の 習慣[しゅうかん]が よく わからなくて 困[こま]った。
Just after I arrived in Japan, I had trouble because I didn't understand Japanese customs very well.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: V-plain.past ばかり indicates that someone has just done something or something has just happened. The noun modification form is ばかりの. --- 英訳 [English translation]: have just V-ed --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-plain.past ばかりだ V-plain.past ばかりの N
この クラスは、 田中[たなか]さん 以外[いがい]は、 誰[だれ]も 外国[がいこく]に 行[い]った ことが ない そうだ。
I heard that, except for Ms. Tanaka, no one in this class has been around.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
{N/DemP} 以外に "Besides N/DemP" X以外に means "besides X" and に is sometimes omitted.
寿司[すし]が 嫌[きら]いな 日本[にほん]人[じん]なんて 聞[き]いた ことが ない。 (=～などと いう 人[ひと]は)
lit= I have never heard of someone like a Japanese person who doesn't like sushi. meaning = I've never heard of a Japanese person who doesn't like sushi.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: (1) Sentence など(は) is an abbreviated form of S などということは, which means "things like S." (2) Noun など(は) is a shortened form of Noun などという{もの/人/etc.}は, which means "things/people/etc. like N." なんで is a colloquial version of など(は). (3) When S is a quotation, Sなどと is an abbreviated form of S などということを. --- 英訳 [English translation]: things/people/etc. like ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N{など(は)/なんて}: 子供{など(は)/なんて}
この 仕事[しごと]は 危険[きけん]でも あれば 大変[たいへん]でも ある。 しかし、 誰[だれ]かが やらなければならないのだ。
This work is both dangerous and difficult, but somebody has to do it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

ANa {に／で} も V-cond ば、〜も "some do ~ and others do ~; do ~ and ~ among other things; sometimes ~ and sometimes ~; there are times when ~ and times when ~; ~ and also ~; ~ and ~ as well" This structure is used to present actions or states (usually 2) as examples of possible or past actions/states. In many cases the actions/states are contrastive ones.
挨拶[あいさつ]の 仕方[しかた]にも 文化[ぶんか]の 違[ちが]いが 見[み]られます。
One can observe cultural differences in the way people greet each other, too.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 見られる is the passive form of 見る and means "be observed." 見られる can also be interpreted as the potential form of 見る, in which case it means "can observe/see" --- 英訳 [English translation]: (something) is observed; (one) can observe/see --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nが見られる
この 荷物[にもつ]は 重[おも]すぎて 誰[だれ]も 持[も]ち上[あ]げる ことは 出来[でき]ない。
This bag is to heavy for anyone to pick up, but if we had a machine we'd be able to lift it easily.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

持ち上げる transitive "1: to elevate; to raise; to lift up; 2: to flatter; to extol; to praise to the sky" Affixed to the end of masu-stems of verbs, 上げる forms compound verbs, adding meanings such as "finish something up," "upward," or "to a great extent." The meaning is determined by the preceeding verb.
結構[けっこう] 上手[じょうず]に 書[か]く； 結構[けっこう] 誰[だれ]とでも 話[はな]す； 結構[けっこう] 昔[むかし]から ある
to write fairly well; to talk with pretty much anyone; to have been, since a pretty long time ago
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
結構 Verb Phrase Means: fairly; pretty; rather; quite The adverb 結構 indicates that the speaker feels that the degree/level/amount/etc. of something is not high, but is higher than average
日本[にほん]の 食[た]べ物[もの]の 中[なか]では、 寿司[すし]や てんぷらなどが 好[す]きです。
Among Japanese foods, I like sushi, tempura and others.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: など indicates that the given list is not exhaustive. When more than one item is listed, や is commonly used to connect the item. --- 英訳 [English translation]: N1やN2など = N1, N2 and others. N1やN2などのN3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. N1やN2など、N3 = N3 such as N1 and N2; N3 like N1 and N2. --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N1やN2など({は / も / が / を / に / の / etc.)} (N1 and N2 can be words or phrases).
この クラスには キムさんの 他[ほか]に (も) 韓国[かんこく]語[ご]が 出来[でき]る 学生[がくせい]が ありますか。
Are there any students in this class besides Kim who can speak Korean?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Nの他に(も) is an adverbial phrase meaning "in addition to N." Verbs, adjectives and demonstrative adjectives can also precede 他に(も) to mean "in addition to V-ing," "in addition to being Adj." or "in addition to this/that." ~他(に)は also means "in addition to." In some contexts, the phrase can mean "except for; other than" --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~他に(も) = in addition to ~; besides ~他(に)は(~ない) = (not ~) except for ~; (not~) other than ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~他に(も); ~他(に)は {この/その/あの}他に(も)
日本[にほん]の トイレには、 お湯[ゆ]が お尻[しり]を 洗[あら]う トイレから、 ふたが 自動[じどう]で 開[ひら]く トイレまでも ある。
There are Japanese toilets that wash your bottom with warm water and even those that have self-opening lids.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N1 から N2 までも "even; to even" までも is used to present something which is considered to be beyond one's expectation or imagination.
将来[しょうらい]は、 誰[だれ]でも 宇宙[うちゅう] 旅行[りょこう]が できる ようになると いう ことは、 考[かんが]えられない ことでは ありません。
It's not onconceivable that, in the future, anyone can take a spacetrip.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N {は／なんて} 考えられない "unimaginable; inconceivable; unthinkable"
「男[おとこ]らしい」とか 「女[おんな]らしい」と いう 言葉[ことば]は、 あまり 好[す]きでは ありません。 誰[だれ]でも、 その 人[ひと]らしく 生[い]きればいいのでは ないでしょうか。
I don't like words such as "manly" or "womanly" very much. Shouldn't people live just as they are?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N らしい means that something/someone is representative of N. and XはNらしい conveys the idea that X has the positive characteristics of N. NOTE: らしい is an i-adjective so the noun-mod and adverbial forms are らしい and らしく respectively.
子供[こども]の 頃[ころ]は、 毎年[まいとし]の ように 夏休[なつやす]みに 海[うみ]に 行[い]っていた。
When I was a child, we went to the ocean almost every year during summer break.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The literal meaning of this phrase is "like every ~," but it is used to mean "almost every ~." --- 英訳 [English translation]: almost every ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ 毎Xのように (X = time word): 毎{日/週/月/年/回}のように
この 大学[だいがく]には、 韓国[かんこく]、 中国[ちゅうごく]、 台湾[たいわん]、と いった アジアの 国々[くにぐに]からの 留学[りゅうがく]生[せい]が たくさん いる。
There are many international students from Asian countries such as Korea, China, and Taiwan at this university.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

N1 {や／、} N2 {や／、} といった {N/NP} "like; such as N" といった X is used to present examples of X. X is always a noun or noun phrase. といった may be preceded by nouns, noun phrases and sentences. * If preceded by nouns, 2+ nouns are presented ** If preceded by sentences or phrases, only one sentence or phrase is presented. などのN and のような N are similar in meaning, but they are usually not preceded by sentences.
A) 田中[たなか]さんは、 明日[あした]の 会議[かいぎ]に 出[で]られない そうですよ。 B) すると、 誰[だれ]か 他[ほか]の 人[ひと]が 出[で]なくては いけないと いう ことですね。
A) I heard Tanaka-san will be unable to come to tomorrow's meeting. B) Then, that means that somebody else will have to go, doesn't it?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
S1. すると、S2. "then" すると connects two sentences S1 and S2 in three situations. In this particular case, it is (3) From the information implied in S1, the speaker confirms that S2 is the case.
子供[こども]の 頃[ころ] 嫌[きら]いであった 食[た]べ物[もの]が、 大人[おとな]に なって 好[す]きになると いう 話[はなし]を よく 聞[き]く。
One often hears stories about disliking food as a child, but coming to like it as an adult.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{〜である/ ~であった} / {~ではない/~ではなかった} である is the formal plain form of だ and can be affixed to nouns and -な／-の adjectives. である is used in formal writing. In very formal speech the polite form であります／ではありません may be used. である can occur before nouns in relative clauses while だ cannot.
日本[にほん]人[じん]が 大好[だいす]きな 桜[さくら]の 花[はな]が いつ頃[ごろ] 咲[さ]くかは、 場所[ばしょ]に よって 違[ちが]います。
The approximate blooming time for Sakura, beloved by the Japanese, differs depending on location
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
子供[こども]の 頃[ころ]は、 毎年[まいとし] 夏休[なつやす]みに なると、 家族[かぞく]と 海[うみ]に 泳[およ]ぎに 行[い]った ものだ。
When I was a child, I used to go swimming at the shore with my family every year during summer vacation.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-plain.non-past ものだ "used to ~; would" V-plain.past ものだ is used to describe in a nostalgic fashion what someone did or what happened in the past
昨日[きのう]、 日本[にほん]で 大[おお]きい 地震[じしん]が あったらしいですね。 田中[たなか]さんの ご家族[かぞく]は 大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]でしょうか。
I heard that there was a big earthquake in Japan yesterday. Is your family all right, Ms. Tanaka?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

〜らしい。 Means: seem; apparently; I heard that ~; it looks like The auxiliary i-adjective らしい is used to express the speaker's conjecture based on what he/she has learned through an information source or his/her own observation
昭和[しょうわ] 25[にじゅうご]年[ねん] 頃[ころ]、 すなわち 1950[せんきゅうひゃくごじゅう]年[ねん] 頃[ころ]の 日本[にほん]は、 戦争[せんそう]が 終[お]わった すぐ 後[あと]で、 みんな 貧乏[びんぼう]だった。
Around the 25th year of Showa, that is, 1950, the war had just ended and everyone in Japan was poor.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
NP1/S1, すなわち NP2/S2 "that is; i.e.; namely" すなわち
日本[にほん]人[じん]は 自分[じぶん]の 家族[かぞく]の ことを 誰[だれ]かに 話[はな]す 時[とき]、 あまり いい ことを 言[い]わない 傾向[けいこう]が ある。
Japanese people tend not to say good things when talking about their family members.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

{V/A}-plain.nonpast (という)傾向がある。 Means: Have a tendency to; have an inclination to; There is a tendency to; tend to This construction is used when someone or something has a tendency to do something. It is commonly used in written language and formal speech. という is optional.
私[わたし]は 辛[つら]い 食[た]べ物[もの]が 好[す]きだから、 どちらかと いうと 日本[にほん]語[ご] 料理[りょうり]より、 韓国[かんこく] 料理[りょうり]の 方[ほう]が 好[す]きだ。
I like spicy food, so if I had to pick, I'd say I like Korean food more than Japanese food.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
どちらかというと "if anything; rather; if I have to decide" This is a set phrase.
あの レストランは 週末[しゅうまつ]は 沈[ちん] 混[こ]んでいるけど、 今日[きょう]は 水曜[すいよう] 日[び]だから、 予約[よやく] なしでも 大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]だろう。
That restaurant is busy on weekends, but it's Wednesday today, so we should be all right without a reservation.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
N なし で V "without ~; with no ~"
高校[こうこう]生[せい]の 頃[ころ]は、 学校[がっこう]の 帰[かえ]りがけに 友達[ともだち]と 映画[えいが]を 見[み]たり、 本屋[ほんや]に 行[い]ったり した ものです。
When I was in high school, I used to do things like see movies with friends and go to the bookstore on the way home from school.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
V-masu がけに "on one's way" がけに is used with the masu-stem of motion verbs like 行く、来る、and 帰る to mean "on one's way."
日本[にほん]の お城[しろ]と 言[い]えば、 姫路[ひめじ]城[じょう]や 大阪[おおさか]城[じょう]が 有名[ゆうめい]だ。 全種[ぜんしゅ]は 兵庫[ひょうご]県[けん]に あって、 後者[こうしゃ]は 大阪[おおさか]府[ふ]に ある。
When it comes to Japanese castles, Himeji Castle and Osaka Castle are famous. The former is in Hyogo prefecture and the latter is in Osaka prefecture.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
前者は（〜）{V-te/A-te/ANa で/N で/}、後者は〜 "The former ~, and the latter ~" This sentence structure is used to refer separately to the two things, people, etc. mentioned in the previous sentence.
此[こ]の 本[ほん]の 良[よ]さが 良[よ]く 分[わ]かる。
I know well the "goodness"/merit/virtue of this book.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix さ is attached to the stem of an i-adjective or a na-adjective to form a noun. The typical effect is the addition of this suffix "-ness," as in "niceness" or "-ty," as in "rarity." --- 英訳 [English translation]: -ness; -ty --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {A-stem / ANa} + さ: ひろい + さ = ひろさ; さむい + さ = さむさ; 元気さ; 便利さ; (Exception: いい = よさ)
此[こ]れは チョコレートの ように 見[み]えるけれど、 消[け]し ゴムだから、 食[た]べられませんよ。
You can see that this looks like chocolate, but it is an eraser, so you can't eat it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように is used when (1) X resembles Y, (2) when X is as Y shows, says, explains, etc. or (3) when X does something as shown/said/explained, etc. in/by Y. --- 英訳 [English translation]: like; as; as if --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N のように V-plain ように
此[こ]の 荷物[にもつ]の 重[おも]さは 何[なん]キロくらいでしょうか。
Around how many kilos is the weight of this bag? / I wonder how heavy this bag is
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix さ is attached to the stem of an i-adjective or a na-adjective to form a noun. The typical effect is the addition of this suffix "-ness," as in "niceness" or "-ty," as in "rarity." --- 英訳 [English translation]: -ness; -ty --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {A-stem / ANa} + さ: ひろい + さ = ひろさ; さむい + さ = さむさ; 元気さ; 便利さ; (Exception: いい = よさ)
此[こ]の 皿[さら]は プラスチックで、 そして、 此[こ]の コップは 紙[かみ]で 出来[でき]ている。
This plate is made from plastic, and this cup is made from paper.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: {で/から}できる means "to be made of/from/out of." から indicates that the material(s) from which something is made is not immediately obvious. できる is used in generic statements while できている is used when describing something specific. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~でできる = be made of; be made out of ~からできる = be made from --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N {で / から} {できる / できている} --- The difference between raw material and material/ingredient is whether the material undergoes qualitative transformation in the production process. Typically, when there is a qualitative change, から is used; when there is no qualitative change, で is used.
どの 大学[だいがく]に 留学[りゅうがく] するかは、 貰[もら]える 奨学[しょうがく]金[きん]に よる。
Where (lit. at what university) I study abroad depends on how big a scholarship I can get.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: This structure is used to indicate that something differs depending on the situation, location, time, etc. --- 英訳 [English translation]: ~によって違う = differ depending on ~ / due to ~ による = depend on, due to, according to --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {Noun/Question Word ~ か/ ~かどうか}は Noun に {よって違う / よる }
其[そ]の 映画[えいが]は 面白[おもしろ]いだけじゃなくて、 音楽[おんがく]も いいよ。
Not only is the movie interesting, but also the film's music is good.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The sentence structures ~だけでなく、~も, etc. expresses the idea "not only X, but also Y." Particles に, へ, で, と or から may appear before も. --- 英訳 [English translation]: not only ~, but also ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Noun だけでなく、Noun(Particle) も b. Subject だけでなく、Noun(Particle) も: Type 2c
此[こ]の 話[はなし]の 良[よ]さが 分[わ]からない 人[ひと]は 居[い]ないと 思[おも]います。
I don't think there's anyone who wouldn't understand the merit of this story.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The suffix さ is attached to the stem of an i-adjective or a na-adjective to form a noun. The typical effect is the addition of this suffix "-ness," as in "niceness" or "-ty," as in "rarity." --- 英訳 [English translation]: -ness; -ty --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ {A-stem / ANa} + さ: ひろい + さ = ひろさ; さむい + さ = さむさ; 元気さ; 便利さ; (Exception: いい = よさ)
此処[ここ]に 「静[しず]かにして下[くだ]さい」って 書[か]いて有[あ]るのが 見[み]えませんか。
Please be quiet is written right here, can't you see it?
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: って is the informal colloquial form of the quotative marker と. って commonly occurs with verbs like 言う, 聞く, 書く and 呼ぶ. --- 英訳 [English translation]: (tell, hear, say, etc.) that ~ Noun1っていうNoun2 = Noun2 called Noun1 --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Sって{言う/聞く/書く} b. Nって{言う/聞く/呼ぶ} c. N1っていうN2
此[こ]の お寺[てら]は 古[ふる]い 桜[さくら]の 木[き]が 有[あ]る 事[こと]で 有名[ゆうめい]だ。
This temple is famous for its old cherry blossom trees.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: Either a noun or a sentence (S + こと) occurs before で to state what X is famous for or the reason that X is famous. --- 英訳 [English translation]: X is famous for Y; X is known because --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ ~は N で {有名です / 知られている} ~は S こと で {有名です / 知られている}
此[こ]の 地方[ちほう]では、 １１[じゅういち]月[がつ]に 成[な]ると 雪[ゆき]が 降[ふ]り始[はじ]めます。
When it turns November in this region, snow begins to fall.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate
説明 [explanation]: 始める in this use is an auxiliary verb meaning "begin to V." --- 英訳 [English translation]: begin to, begin-V-ing --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Verb-masu 始める
此[こ]れは、 １[いち]年[ねん]生[せい]の 学生[がくせい]に 良[よ]く 見[み]られる 間違[まちが]いです。
This is a mistake that can often be observed among first year students.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: 見られる is the passive form of 見る and means "be observed." 見られる can also be interpreted as the potential form of 見る, in which case it means "can observe/see" --- 英訳 [English translation]: (something) is observed; (one) can observe/see --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ Nが見られる
此[こ]の 写真[しゃしん]を 見[み]れば 分[わ]かる ように、 ロンドンには、 色々[いろいろ]な 名所[めいしょ]が 有[あ]る。
As you can see if you look at these photos, there are various famous locations in London.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように is used when (1) X resembles Y, (2) when X is as Y shows, says, explains, etc. or (3) when X does something as shown/said/explained, etc. in/by Y. --- 英訳 [English translation]: like; as; as if --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N のように V-plain ように
此[こ]の 本[ほん]に 書[か]いて有[あ]る ように 作[つく]れば、 美味[おい]しい ドレッシングが 出来[でき]るよ。
You can make delicious dressing if you follow the recipe in this book (lt. make it as if it's written in this book).
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: ように is used when (1) X resembles Y, (2) when X is as Y shows, says, explains, etc. or (3) when X does something as shown/said/explained, etc. in/by Y. --- 英訳 [English translation]: like; as; as if --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ N のように V-plain ように
此[こ]の アパートは 駅[えき]から 近[ちか]くて 便利[べんり]なだけじゃなくて、 家賃[やちん]も 安[やす]いから、 借[か]りる 事[こと]に 為[し]た。
Not only is this apartment conveniently close to the train station, but also the rent is cheap, so I've decided to rent it.
Grammar,扉,Intermediate

説明 [explanation]: The sentence structures ~だけでなく、~も, etc. expresses the idea "not only X, but also Y." Particles に, へ, で, と or から may appear before も. --- 英訳 [English translation]: not only ~, but also ~ --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ a. Noun だけでなく、Noun(Particle) も b. Subject だけでなく、Noun(Particle) も: Type 2c

X にもかかわらず Y where X is {V/A}-plain ANa {な／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} N {の／じゃない／だった／じゃなかった} "in spite of (the fact that ~); despite (the fact that ~); although; though; nevertheless" This construction is used to mean "Y in spite of X." It is used when Y is the case even though Y is not usually expected from X.
昨日[きのう]は 友達[ともだち]と レストランで 晩御飯[ばんごはん]を 食[た]べ、 其[そ]の 後[ご]、 映画[えいが]を 見[み]に 行[い]った。
Yesterday I ate dinner at a restaurant with a friend, and after that we went to see a movie.

説明 [explanation]: The masu stem of a verb and the stem of an i-adjective + く indicate that the sentence is continuing. That is, they function like the English sentence connector "and." This use is generally restricted to written language. In spoken language the te-form of a verb or an i-adjective is commonly used. --- 英訳 [English translation]: and --- 文型 [sentence pattern]:​ V-masu、 ~ A-stem + く、 ~
